app.name: Video API
app.summary: Editors upload videos, fill in their details and publish them. Viewers browse the catalog, open a video's page and play it. Every open and play is counted.

glossary.meaning: A video that was uploaded but not published yet. Every new video starts here.
A video an editor made live.
A deleted video. It is kept in the database but hidden from every flow.
Title, synopsis, director, cast, year of release, genre and running time.
Where the video file lives (a link or path).
One opening of the video's details page.

excluded.reason: Generated API documentation (OpenAPI), not product behavior

flows.title: Upload a video
flows.summary: An editor sends the location of a video file. The video is created as a draft with empty details, ready to be filled in and published.

calls.note: POST /videos/upload routed by Spring MVC mapping annotation

nodes.label: Was the video's content included?
nodes.rule: The request must include the content field (where the file lives). Only a missing field is rejected: empty text is accepted.

calls.note: @Valid runs bean validation before the controller method

nodes.label: Create the video as a draft
nodes.rule: Every new video starts as Draft, with empty details, 0 views and 0 impressions.

nodes.label: Draft video created
nodes.response: 200 · the new video and its id

findings.text: A video uploaded with empty content can never be published, and nothing lets an editor change the content later. The only way out is to delete it and upload again.

flows.title: Edit a video's details
flows.summary: An editor fills in or corrects a video's title, synopsis, director, cast, year, genre or running time. Only the fields sent are changed.

calls.note: PATCH /videos/{id}/metadata routed by Spring MVC mapping annotation

nodes.label: Are the year and running time valid?
nodes.rule: Year of release must be 1878 or later (the year of the first film). Running time must be written as HH:mm:ss, for example 01:45:00. A request with any field the API doesn't know is also refused.

nodes.label: Does the video exist and is it not deleted?
nodes.rule: Archived (deleted) videos are treated as if they don't exist.

nodes.label: Apply only the fields that were sent
nodes.rule: Fields left out keep their current value, and an empty cast list is ignored. A field can't be cleared once it has a value. This works the same for drafts and published videos.

calls.note: content is always null here, so it never changes
status is null here, so it never changes

nodes.label: Edit refused: invalid year or running time

findings.text: Details of a published video can be changed at any time, with no review step. A live video's title can change without being published again.
A field can't be removed once filled in: leaving it out keeps the old value.

flows.title: Publish a video
flows.summary: An editor makes a draft video live. The video must have content and complete details first.

calls.note: PATCH /videos/{id}/publish routed by Spring MVC mapping annotation

nodes.label: Does the video exist and is it not deleted?
nodes.rule: Archived (deleted) videos are treated as if they don't exist.

nodes.label: Is the video still a draft?
nodes.rule: Only Draft videos can be published. Publishing a video that is already published is refused.

nodes.label: Does the video have content?
nodes.rule: The content can't be missing or empty.

nodes.label: Are all the details filled in?
nodes.rule: Six details are required: title, synopsis, director, cast (at least one person), year of release and genre. Running time is optional.

nodes.label: Refused: video is not a draft
nodes.response: 400 · Video must be in DRAFT status to be published

nodes.label: Refused: video has no content
nodes.response: 400 · Video must have content to be published

findings.text: A draft with empty content is stuck here forever, because no flow can add content after upload.

flows.title: Unpublish a video
flows.summary: An editor takes a live video down without deleting it. It goes back to Draft, so viewers stop seeing it and it can be published again.

calls.note: PATCH /videos/{id}/unpublish routed by Spring MVC mapping annotation

nodes.label: Does the video exist and is it not deleted?
nodes.rule: Archived (deleted) videos are treated as if they don't exist.

nodes.label: Is the video published?
nodes.rule: Only published videos can be unpublished. Drafts are refused.

nodes.label: Move the video back to draft
nodes.rule: Views, impressions and details are kept.

nodes.label: Refused: video is not published
nodes.response: 400 · Only published videos can be unpublished

findings.text: The response reuses the publish response, so apps see the same shape for both actions. Nothing tells viewers who saved the link; it now answers "not found".

flows.title: Play a video
flows.summary: A viewer presses play. The video's content is returned and one view is counted.

calls.note: GET /videos/{id}/play routed by Spring MVC mapping annotation

nodes.label: Does the video exist and is it not deleted?
nodes.rule: Archived (deleted) videos are treated as if they don't exist.

nodes.label: Is the video published?
nodes.rule: Only published videos can be played by viewers. Drafts answer as if they don't exist.

nodes.label: Count one view
nodes.rule: Every play request adds 1 view, including repeated plays by the same person. Nothing checks who is watching.

findings.text: Views are counted on every request, so refreshes and bots inflate the numbers.

flows.title: Open a video's page
flows.summary: A viewer opens a video's page. All its details, counts and status are returned and one impression is counted.

calls.note: GET /videos/{id}/load routed by Spring MVC mapping annotation

nodes.label: Does the video exist and is it not deleted?
nodes.rule: Archived (deleted) videos are treated as if they don't exist.

nodes.label: Is the video published?
nodes.rule: Only published videos can be opened by viewers. Drafts answer as if they don't exist.

nodes.label: Count one impression
nodes.rule: Every page open adds 1 impression, including repeated opens by the same person.

nodes.label: Page shows details, counts and status

flows.title: Search the catalog
flows.summary: A viewer lists or searches videos. All filters are optional. Results show a short summary of each video.

calls.note: GET /videos routed by Spring MVC mapping annotation

nodes.label: Filter by what the viewer typed
nodes.rule: Filters are optional and all must match. Title, director and genre match any part of the text, ignoring case. Year must match exactly. Cast must match one person's full name, ignoring case.

nodes.label: Read matching published videos
nodes.rule: Only published videos appear. Drafts and deleted videos are hidden.

nodes.label: List of matching videos
nodes.response: 200 · id, title, synopsis, director, main actor, genre

calls.note: once per video; main actor = first cast member

findings.text: Code comments describe the cast filter as a partial match, or as unused. In practice it needs a person's exact full name.
Open question left in the code: should showing a video in search results count an impression? Today it doesn't.
There is no paging: every match is returned at once.

flows.title: Delete a video
flows.summary: An editor removes a video. It is archived rather than erased, and disappears from every other flow.

calls.note: DELETE /videos/{id} routed by Spring MVC mapping annotation

nodes.label: Does the video exist and is it not deleted?
nodes.rule: Archived (deleted) videos are treated as if they don't exist, so deleting twice returns 'not found'.

nodes.label: Archive the video
nodes.rule: The video is marked Archived, not erased. Its details and counts stay in the database.

outcomes.not-found: Video not found or already deleted

findings.text: A deleted video can't be restored. Nothing in the app moves a video out of Archived.
